item.title: Courvoisier Brought Back The Classic House Party With Coi Leray And A Strict No Phones Rule
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Courvoisier revived Manhattan nightlife nostalgia as Coi Leray joined a celebrity reunion celebrating personal bonds beyond digital screens.
item.content:encoded:
Courvoisier brought old school house party culture back to New York City with a phone free mansion takeover and a star studded gathering featuring Coi Leray. And AllHipHop was in the house.

The luxury cognac brand traded social media distractions for genuine human interaction during two events Oct. 21 and 22, celebrating the launch of its first global advertising campaign in nearly 20 years.

The centerpiece was House of Courvoisier, an immersive celebration held Oct. 22 at Ideal Glass Studios in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village neighborhood. Guests surrendered access to their phones before entering a two story venue transformed into an elaborate house party.

Working alongside New York collectives Fun With Friends and Missing Ingredient, Courvoisier recreated the atmosphere of a familiar neighborhood gathering with a sophisticated twist.

The space featured a living room, kitchen, game room stocked with Jenga and Uno, a confessional room and an upstairs bedroom hangout. Instead of recording every interaction, attendees were encouraged to dance, socialize and enjoy the festivities without screens competing for their attention.

The concept was simple: The best moments at a party might be the ones nobody records.

The festivities actually began a day earlier when former BET “106 & Park” personalities Terrence J and Rocsi Diaz reunited at Courvoisier’s Living Room Pop-Up at Fosun Plaza in Lower Manhattan.

Hundreds gathered for the public event, which transformed an outdoor plaza into a casual setting for conversations about culture, community and hospitality.

Rapper Coi Leray made a surprise appearance, adding some star power to the reunion of the two television personalities whose years hosting “106 & Park” connected them to generations of Hip-Hop audiences. 

Both events supported “Pass The Courvoisier,” a global campaign developed with BBDO Paris and directed by Grammy Award winner Ibra Ake.

The campaign’s accompanying film follows a bottle of Courvoisier as it travels between guests during a lively Atlanta house party. Cooking, gaming, dancing and spontaneous conversations create the backdrop for a message about companionship.

The campaign also carries a recognizable connection to Hip-Hop history. Its name recalls Busta Rhymes’ 2001 hit “Pass the Courvoisier,” which helped establish the cognac’s place in popular music culture. 

Those findings helped explain why the company chose familiar living spaces rather than traditional nightlife settings for its New York launch.

For a cognac brand whose relationship with Hip-Hop stretches back decades, the campaign represents a return to the social traditions that helped make it recognizable in the first place.

And in a city where nearly every celebrity appearance becomes instant social media content, Courvoisier offered a different proposition: Come inside, put the phone away and give the people around you your undivided attention.

Perhaps the biggest luxury of the evening was being present enough to remember the party without needing a video to prove you were there.

item.title: Boyz II Men Head To Country With Warner Records Nashville Deal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Boyz II Men signed with Warner Records Nashville for a 2027 country project, building on years of country collaborations.
item.content:encoded:
Boyz II Men signed with Warner Records Nashville for a country project due in 2027, marking a new chapter after decades of R&B hits.

Nathan Morris, Wanya Morris and Shawn Stockman told The Tennessean that their first country album grew out of their love for the music. The trio worked with Nashville songwriters for the project. For them, the move was a chance to learn, reach more listeners and keep the sound that built their career.

Stockman pointed to country’s storytelling through song as part of the draw. He named Travis Tritt, Vince Gill and The Chicks among the acts they enjoyed growing up. He also said the new writing sessions helped refresh their creativity and that the Warner team understood their vision.

“We’ve always been enamored with the storytelling component of country music and how they actually put those stories to melody. Again, it was a learning experience. That is what we like. We have been in this business for three decades, but we’ll forever be students of music and we’ll always be open to learn and to appreciate different styles,” Stockman said.

Warner Records Nashville chair and president Cris Lacy welcomed the group in a statement reported by MusicRow. She cited their influence on country artists and their own early love of Randy Travis as reasons the pairing made sense.

“Boyz II Men’s global influence is decades in the making,” Lacy said.

The deal followed their Lady A collaboration, “I Love The One.” That song was made for a forthcoming music project inspired by the series “The Chosen.”

Their ties to Nashville go back years. In a 2019 interview with Nashville Lifestyles, the group spoke about working with Brett Young on “CMT Crossroads” and visiting the Grand Ole Opry. They had also worked on “Be Still Moses” with Steep Canyon Rangers.

Those projects put their voices alongside country and roots acts well before this label deal.

In April, they joined Cody Johnson at Stagecoach in Indio, California. Johnson began singing “On Bended Knee” before the trio came out to help perform their 1994 hit.

The Philadelphia group’s debut, Cooleyhighharmony, arrived in 1991. Their catalog grew to include “End of the Road,” “I’ll Make Love To You” and “Water Runs Dry.” They have won four Grammys and sold more than 60 million albums worldwide.

AllHipHop previously reported on their plans for a biopic and documentary, with the members serving as executive producers alongside partners Compelling Pictures and Primary Wave.

As Wanya explained to The Tennessean, the country album leaves room for the group’s R&B roots.

“We don’t want to become country. We want to be a part of it,” he said.

item.title: Beyoncé Wants Cécred To Win Skeptics
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Beyoncé said Cécred's appeal should come from the haircare products themselves, even for shoppers who disliked her music.
item.content:encoded:
Beyoncé wanted Cécred to reach “the people who can’t stand my music.”

In i-D’s public interview preview, she described a goal of winning customers through results. She discussed the brand with interviewer Eni Subair. She said she was Cécred’s sole investor.

“I’m the founder, visionary, and sole investor, not the face or model for this brand. I had a vision to build something that solved real problems and performed so incredibly that the people who can’t stand my music still use Cécred, because it work,” she said.

That approach was part of her plan from the start. In her 2024 GQ interview, Beyoncé said she kept herself out of Cécred’s launch ads. She wanted customers to judge the products without her fame doing the work.

“My mother and I poured decades of experience, tradition, and love into Cécred, so seeing our community grow across every ethnicity, texture, generation, and gender is so fulfilling. In the beginning, it took some conditioning from the world’s perception of how to launch a brand founded by someone like me,” Beyoncé said.

She also described a double standard in business. Men could be seen as the decision-makers. Famous women were often treated as marketing faces. She said she wanted her work on the products to matter.

She wanted to build something that could earn respect on its own, rather than depend on her name.

Her tie to haircare went back much further than the launch.

Before Cécred had a public name, Beyoncé spoke about growing up around her mother’s salon. She said her first job involved sweeping up hair, and Destiny’s Child sang for clients as they sat for appointments.

She also recalled the entrepreneurial women she met at the salon. She cited that experience while explaining the line’s roots.

As AllHipHop reported when she announced Cécred in February 2024, the launch trailer paired scenes of Beyoncé washing her hair with childhood footage of her and her mother, Tina Knowles.

The announcement set February 20 as the start date. It followed a May 2023 teaser in which she had connected the business to her mother’s work.

That family role extended into product development. Space NK’s Cécred page identified Tina as vice chairwoman and described her involvement in salon testing.

The retailer said she brought four decades of work to the brand. That included her roles as a hairstylist, salon owner and entrepreneur.

Cécred was also on sale through Space NK’s UK site, with shampoo, conditioner, hair oil and styling products listed.

The options included a scalp scrub, detangling spray and heat styling mist. The range covered wash routines, protective styles and extensions, according to the retailer. The retailer also offered the line in stores.

item.title: Jay-Z Confirms Himself For Super Bowl Halftime Show At SoFi Stadium
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Jay-Z was confirmed for his first Super Bowl halftime performance, bringing him back to SoFi Stadium after his anniversary concerts.
item.content:encoded:
Jay-Z will get his own turn on the Super Bowl halftime stage after years of helping other stars put their shows together.

The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday that he will headline Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

It will be his first Super Bowl halftime performance. His company has worked on the show since 2019, but the rapper had yet to take that stage himself.

“Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true,” Jay-Z said.

The announcement settled a question that had followed him into his recent Los Angeles concerts.

Earlier reports pointed to Jay-Z as the pick, but the NFL and Roc Nation had not confirmed those reports at the time.

He had already explained why he waited. During a 2024 interview with Entertainment Tonight, Jay-Z said,

“I thought it would be selfish to pick myself too early.” He added, “Maybe one year.”

Those comments came at the premiere of “The Book of Clarence,” as Usher prepared to perform at that year’s game.

Roc Nation had helped bring acts including Rihanna and The Weeknd to halftime while its founder stayed behind the scenes.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said his initial agreement with Roc Nation came with a request that Jay-Z eventually perform when he felt ready.

The booking now puts the company’s founder in the same headlining role it has helped other artists fill.

Hip-Hop had a large presence the last time the game came to the Los Angeles area.

The 2022 halftime show featured Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige and Kendrick Lamar, with appearances by 50 Cent and Anderson .Paak.

The new date also extends a busy stretch built around his catalog. This year’s concerts celebrated 30 years of Reasonable Doubt and 25 years of The Blueprint.

The run took him to Yankee Stadium, London and Paris before his October 23 and 24 shows at SoFi.

He will return to that same venue for the Super Bowl less than four months after those concerts.

item.title: OMB Peezy Says Rap Success Hasn’t Stopped Him From Feeling Lonely
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: OMB Peezy said he still felt lonely despite his success and explained why he turned to the microphone when he needed to talk.
item.content:encoded:
OMB Peezy said rap success hadn’t spared him from loneliness, and he said he turned to the microphone when he needed to talk.

In an interview with Men’s Journal, the Alabama rapper pushed back on the idea that making it in music meant endless cash and a life with no problems. He spoke with writer Annmarie Gajdos in New York City.

“I get lonely all the time,” Peezy said.

Asked who he called in those moments, he answered, “The microphone.” He described recording as a way to bring out feelings and memories he had put aside.

“Every album is like therapy for real,” he said.

His latest project, Save Yourself, arrived October 16 through Overkill Ent. The album includes “Language Barrier,” “Stay Away From Me,” and “Save Your Life,” which draws on The Fray’s “How to Save a Life.” Trap Dickey joined him on “What She Wants,” which reworks TLC’s “No Scrubs.”

That use of the booth as a place to vent has roots in his earlier work. During a 2021 interview with AllHipHop about Too Deep For Tears, Peezy explained that he had moved past simply touching on pain. He wanted listeners to know the specific things he had lived through.

“I always been going through sh-t since a youngin’. Whenever I get in a situation, I say “Sh-t, f-ck it.” If I know I can’t change the situation or I know I couldn’t prevent the situation from happening, “sh-t f-ck it. It is what it is.,” Peezy said.

The sessions could get personal enough that he wanted the room dark. He recalled switching off the booth light while making “Soul Ties” and “I Try” because he did not want people watching his face as he worked through his feelings.

Peezy also said he kept recording through the pandemic until most of his planned tracklist had changed. Only two songs from the original list remained. Life events kept giving him new things to address on record.

More recently, in a statement accompanying Save Yourself, he said he had spent roughly a year and a half making changes. That included changing his surroundings and working to shift the way people saw him.

In the new interview, Peezy said he prayed for peace and felt he was beginning to find it. His advice was to spend time alone with the television off and the phone put away.

item.title: Playboi Carti’s X Bio Raises Hack Questions After Meme Coin Rush
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Playboi Carti's X bio drew hack questions as a CARTI token sank, while his connection to the coin remained unconfirmed.
item.content:encoded:
Playboi Carti‘s X bio sparked a meme coin rush on Sunday, October 25, as traders chased tokens with his name and later questioned who changed the account.

A Pump.fun reference appeared on his profile, which had about 3.6 million followers.

A CARTI token later sank, but no confirmed link between the rapper and the coin had been established, according to Bitcoin.com.

Crypto Gorilla, a crypto commentator who documented the change that evening, raised the hacking question from the start.

“PlayboiCarti added PF to his bio (hacked?)” the commentator wrote on X.

The same post said the account hadn’t shared a wallet or contract address identifying a specific token. It also noted that Carti’s last post was dated to early 2025. Several coins using CARTI were trading on the attention around the profile, the commentator said.

In a later recap, Crypto Gorilla said one CARTI token reached about $1.2 million in market value before collapsing. The recap described an apparent hack but did not establish who accessed Carti’s account.

A snapshot at 1:48 P.M. Eastern on Monday showed a Solana token named playboicarti (symbol: carti) down 76.28% over 24 hours. That pair recorded about $4.12 million in trading volume during the period, while its market value stood at $9,779.

Those figures measured different things. Trading volume counted activity across purchases and sales; it did not mean Carti collected $4.12 million or that buyers lost that amount. The listing’s social link pointed to his X page, which by itself did not establish his involvement in the token.

Bitcoin.com also reported that more than 20 CARTI tokens appeared across Solana, Robinhood Chain and Arc. The shared name left traders facing several different coins instead of one verified, artist-backed launch.

Celebrity names and account-access claims have crossed paths in this market before.

AllHipHop previously reported on Iggy Azalea’s promotion of MOTHER in 2024 and Hulk Hogan’s claim that someone hacked his account after it promoted HULK. Hogan publicly distanced himself from those posts.

Bitcoin.com reported no statement from Carti’s team at the time. It remained unclear who changed his bio and whether any token creator had access to his account.

item.title: King Charles Faces Reparations Calls Before Caribbean Tour
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: King Charles III faced calls for a slavery apology and reparations as he prepared to begin his Caribbean tour on October 27.
item.content:encoded:
King Charles III faced fresh calls for slavery reparations and a formal apology as he prepared to start his Caribbean tour on October 27.

Niambi Hall Campbell-Dean, who chairs the Bahamas National Reparations Committee, questioned the monarchy’s place in the country in an interview with The Associated Press. “Why do we still have a king? What does this person really represent to us?” she asked.

Guyana’s President Irfaan Ali told ITV News that Charles’s past acknowledgment of slavery should be followed by an apology and reparatory justice. He also praised the king’s work on forests, climate change and Indigenous rights.

The palace’s plans run from October 27 through November 4, with stops in the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda.

Queen Camilla will join Charles in Antigua and Barbuda, where they will attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. Guyana’s government said Charles would arrive on October 29 for a two-day state visit. His schedule includes a State House meeting with Ali and talks with the National Toshaos Council.

But no formal apology is planned.

Charles acts on UK government advice. A palace spokesperson said he would address past wrongs and enduring inequality during the visit, while host countries’ priorities would guide the program.

The debate also reaches beyond what the king might say on this trip. Barbados replaced Queen Elizabeth II with President Sandra Mason as head of state in 2021, when Charles attended its transition to a republic. The country remained a member of the Commonwealth. Guyana became a republic in 1970 and also stayed in the Commonwealth.

Caribbean Community leaders had already agreed in July to make reparations a visible issue at the November Commonwealth summit. They approved a ten-point reparations manifesto, backed cooperation with the African Union and supported Jamaica’s planned petition to Charles.

Jamaica filed the petition on September 7 and referred it to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. It asks whether the capture, transport and enslavement of Africans in Jamaica were lawful under English law, whether they breached international law and whether Britain owes a remedy.

Jamaican Culture Minister Olivia Grange said a preliminary hearing was set for the week of March 8, 2027, according to the Jamaica Information Service. She said the UK government has until November 20 to file its case.

item.title: French Montana’s Amsterdam, Vienna Concerts Suddenly Canceled
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: French Montana and D-Block Europe's October 30 Amsterdam show was canceled, with Ticketmaster set to contact ticket holders.
item.content:encoded:
French Montana and D-Block Europe’s Amsterdam concert was canceled, leaving fans without the joint show booked for Friday, October 30, at AFAS Live.

The venue confirmed the cancellation on its official event page, citing “unforeseen circumstances.”

“Ticket holders will receive an email from Ticketmaster with further information regarding the cancellation,” AFAS Live said.

The Amsterdam stop was billed as part of the “Worldwide Wave Tour.” Their London date remains on sale.

London’s O2 still lists D-Block Europe with French Montana as a special guest for Wednesday, October 28. The arena’s event page shows tickets on sale through AXS, its official ticket partner. Doors are listed for 6:30 P.M.

Another canceled date on Ticketmaster’s French Montana calendar is the November 6 show with D-Block Europe at Raiffeisen Halle im Gasometer in Vienna. That listing marks the Austrian concert as canceled without giving a reason.

Young Adz and Dirtbike LB formed D-Block Europe in Lewisham, London. They had come close to topping the U.K.’s Official Albums Chart with The Blue Print – Us Vs. Them and Lap 5. Both albums peaked at No. 2.

The duo reached No. 1 in January 2024 with Rolling Stone, their third studio album. It featured Yxng Bane, Noizy and Kodak Black. That success brought their Top 10 album tally to eight at the time, according to Official Charts.

That week, Rolling Stone also led the U.K. sales chart for independent record stores. It entered the vinyl albums chart at No. 2, giving the pair a strong showing with record buyers, too.

French Montana’s recent work also revisited a longtime partnership.

He and Max B announced Wave Gods 2: Cosmos Brothers earlier this year, with a May 22 release, as AllHipHop reported on their reunion. That project included “Smoking Part 2” and reunited two artists who had made music together years before.

French Montana explained that the album’s title grew from Max B’s talk about cosmic energy during calls between the two artists. He also described the music he wanted to make: “I’m all about restoration. I felt like the music business lost that edge, lost that music that people appreciated.”

item.title: Lewis Hamilton Reveals Dog Gift For Kanye & Kim Kardashian’s Four Kids
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Lewis Hamilton said he gave Kim Kardashian's four children a dog named Halo as he shared what brought him joy away from racing.
item.content:encoded:
Lewis Hamilton gave Kim Kardashian‘s four children a dog this year. His name is Halo, and the driver called him part of the family. The Formula 1 star shared the news when asked what brought him joy outside of racing.

Hamilton, 41, spoke at a press panel in Austin, Texas, on Saturday, October 24. He was in town for the F1 Grand Prix. He first mentioned the joy his niece and nephew bring him. He then turned to his girlfriend’s kids and said he loved spending time with them.

“I got them a dog this year, so little Halo is a new member of that family,” he said.

Kardashian shares North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8 and Psalm, 7, with her former husband, Kanye West. The children have also appeared in photos with Hamilton as his relationship with their mother became more public over the summer.

In July, Hamilton posted a photo of himself with Kardashian, Chicago and Psalm. The group posed together by a lake on a summer trip.

Fans had seen Halo in the couple’s social media posts before the Austin event. According to HOLA!, Kardashian shared a photo of herself holding the golden retriever on July 30. Hamilton joined Kardashian and her family on that lakeside trip.

On September 22, Hamilton posted another photo of Halo. This time, the dog had its front paws up on a gate.

The couple’s family outings followed a friendship that became a romance earlier this year. Us Weekly reported that Kardashian introduced Hamilton to her children as the two began dating after knowing each other for years.

For Kardashian, the relationship came after a period she set aside to heal. She said she wanted to put her kids and work first. She told The Times she had felt no rush to date again. She had enjoyed having that space for herself.

Kardashian filed for divorce from West in February 2021. They reached a settlement in November 2022. By June 2026, she was spending more time with Hamilton online. That month, she posted a photo and video from their New York bike ride.

item.title: Drake Honors Lil Wayne At Birthday Party, But Is A Major Reunion Coming?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Drake's emotional birthday tribute to Lil Wayne raises fresh questions about their unreleased collaborations and whether the legendary duo could reunite.
item.content:encoded:
Drake turned 40 over the weekend, but his birthday tribute to Lil Wayne has me wondering whether the next chapter of their legendary partnership is finally approaching.

The Toronto-based superstar celebrated his milestone birthday with lavish festivities in New York City, surrounded by famous friends, family and luxury. But amid the random things happening, Drake got sentimental.

READ ALSO: Drake Turns 40: 40 Things I’ve Learned From Drake

First, he shared a musical moment with his father, Dennis Graham, who arrived sporting a colorful outfit and a parrot on his shoulder. Yes, an actual parrot. Apparently, ordinary birthday accessories are beneath the Graham family.

The father and son performed together, with Dennis revisiting his 2017 song “Kinda Crazy.” It was a touching family moment. That bird deserves an honorable mention.

Then came the big tribute.

“I would not be here if it was not by way and courtesy of the young man Lil Wayne from YMCMB.”

Wayne wasn’t present, but his chi certainly was.

And here’s why I’m paying attention.

Earlier this month, Weezy revealed that he and Drake have a substantial collection of unreleased recordings, including material dating back to 2014 and 2015.

“We have a whole bunch of unreleased material. I go through stuff from 2014 and 2015, like… really unheard stuff,” Wayne said. “I edit stuff up and just send it to his phone so he can hear the new versions of it and get him going.”

Wayne also indicated that Drake has been enthusiastic about potentially releasing those recordings.

READ ALSO: Loe Shimmy Gifts Drake A 1986 Ferrari For His 40th Birthday

Between 2008 and 2013, the two delivered an extraordinary collection of collaborations, including “Miss Me,” “She Will,” “The Motto” and “HYFR.” Wayne helped introduce Drake to the masses, and Drake eventually ascended into global superstardom.

Their last released collaborations arrived in 2021, when they appeared on Nicki Minaj’s “Seeing Green” and Drake’s “You Only Live Twice” alongside Rick Ross.

That’s five years without another major musical reunion.

Could Drake’s birthday reflection signal renewed interest in those unreleased recordings? Perhaps. There’s no confirmed album, single or release date, but Wayne’s recent comments suggest the music remains very much alive.

And personally, I’d rather hear those vintage recordings than watch another round of internet arguments about who won some rap beef.

At 40, Drake has accomplished virtually everything commercially. Revisiting his musical roots with Wayne could provide something those streaming records cannot.

A reunion with the man who helped make it all possible.

Now, somebody please convince Weezy to open that vault.
